## Question 1

The following table summarizes the season information for the five seasons of AMC's *Breaking Bad* show (the last split into two parts). 

a) Tidy up this data and save it to a tibble. Decide for yourself how to handle season 5 (should it be a single observation or two?). For the first and last aired dates, just store the year as a number.

b) Save the tibble you created to a CSV file named "breaking_bad.csv".

![](../../img/breaking_bad_wikipedia.png)

{{< dstart summary="Answer key" >}}

**Part (a)**

Version with one observation for the season five parts

```{r}
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
season <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)
episodes <- c(7, 13, 13, 13, 16)
first_air <- c(2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012)
last_air <- c(2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2013)
network <- "AMC"
breaking_bad <- 
  tibble(season, episodes, first_air, last_air, network)
breaking_bad
```

Version with two separate observations for the season five parts

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
season <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5.1, 5.2)
episodes <- c(7, 13, 13, 13, 8, 8)
first_air <- c(2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013)
last_air <- c(2008, 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013)
network <- "AMC"
breaking_bad <- 
  tibble(season, episodes, first_air, last_air, network)
breaking_bad
```

**Part (b)**

```{r}
#| message: false
#| eval: false

write_csv(breaking_bad, "breaking_bad.csv")
```

{{< dstop >}}

## Question 2

a) Download the [`cereal.csv`](../../data/cereal.csv){download="cereal.csv"} file and save it to your class Project folder.

b) Use \{tidyverse\} to import this file into R as a tibble named `cereal`, using an argument to make the missing values (coded as `"missing"`) into `NA`s.

c) Run your command again but with the `show_col_types = FALSE` argument to suppress the column specification message.

{{< dstart summary="Answer key" >}}

**Part (b)**

```{r}
#| replace_path: ["../../data/", ""]
cereal <- read_csv("../../data/cereal.csv", na = "missing")
cereal

cereal <- read_csv("../../data/cereal.csv", na = "missing", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

{{< dstop >}}

## Question 3

a) Update the `cereal` tibble from Question 2 to make the `type` variable a factor.

b) Tabulate the `type` variable using `data_tabulate()` and plot its discrete distribution using `qplot()`.

c) Describe the `calories` variable using `describe_distribution()` and plot its continuous distribution using `qplot()` and a "histogram" or "boxplot" geom.

d) Plot the covariation of the `calories` and `rating` variables using `qplot()` and a "point" or "jitter" geom.

{{< dstart summary="Answer key" >}}

**Part (a)**

```{r}
cereal$type <- factor(cereal$type)
cereal
```

**Part (b)**

```{r}
library(easystats)
data_tabulate(cereal, type)
```

```{r}
qplot(x = type, data = cereal, geom = "bar")
```

**Part (c)**

```{r}
describe_distribution(cereal, calories)
```

```{r}
qplot(x = calories, data = cereal, geom = "histogram")
```

**Part (d)**

```{r}
qplot(x = calories, y = rating, data = cereal, geom = "point")
qplot(x = calories, y = rating, data = cereal, geom = "jitter")
```
